Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE:CRM) closed at $242.45 on October 19. The stock returned 30.2% over the last 6 months, compared with an 11.6% return for the Insider Monkey Billionaire Index and 8.7% for the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust.

Oracle Corporation (NYSE:ORCL) closed at $129.59 the same day and has gone the other way, shedding more than a quarter of its value over those six months. Two of the largest businesses in enterprise software, pulled apart by half a year of trading. Salesforce sells the system companies run their customer relationships through. Oracle sells databases and rents out the computing capacity that artificial intelligence models are trained on.

READ ALSO: 10 Best Fundamental Stocks to Invest in According to Billionaires

Salesforce (CRM) vs Oracle (ORCL): Which Is a Better Stock to Buy?
What Salesforce Has:

The customer record lives in Salesforce, and so do the workflows the sales and service teams run on top of it. Replacing that means moving years of history and retraining the people who use it daily, which is why a slowing Salesforce is not a shrinking one. It converts about a fifth of revenue into operating profit and produced $14.4 billion of free cash flow in its last financial year.

What it lacks is growth. Revenue rose 10.80% in the most recent quarter, and the company is now buying what it cannot generate, agreeing on October 20 to pay $5.66 billion for the marketing software business Braze. The bigger risk sits in how it charges. Salesforce sells seats, so if software agents take on work that staff used to do, customers need fewer of them.

Both names appear in our 10 Most Promising Cloud Stocks According to Hedge Funds. To see the full ranking, click HERE.

What Oracle Has:

Oracle grew revenue 29.60% in the quarter just reported on a 35.63% operating margin, and underneath that sits the oldest annuity in software. Companies keep their most important records in Oracle databases, and the support that goes with them renews whether or not anything new is bought. That revenue pays for the build. What the market is being asked to price is the newer half, where Oracle rents capacity to companies training artificial intelligence models on contracts signed years in advance.

The build is the risk. Debt reaches 251.72% of equity, more than twice what Salesforce carries, and Oracle finished the past year with levered free cash flow of negative $45.85 billion despite generating a great deal from operations. Renting capacity also earns a thinner margin than licensing software, so faster revenue is not automatically the better business.

title: Why Did Braze Stock Jump?
detail:
Why Did Braze Stock Jump?
Trefis Team

Braze (BRZE) stock rose 51.7% on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, while the S&P 500 gained 0.3%. The gain occurred the same day news reports said Salesforce had agreed to buy the customer-engagement software company for cash. Braze shareholders now know what they would be paid, allowing that price to be measured against the business Salesforce is buying. So how much is Salesforce paying, set against what Braze sells for today?

How Much Is Salesforce Paying For Braze?

News reports on October 20 said Salesforce will pay $47.50 in cash for each Braze share, a 58% premium to the previous close. The same reports valued the deal at $5.66 billion.

For that price, Salesforce would get a company with $834 million of revenue over the twelve months to July 31, 2026, up 27.4% from a year earlier. Over the same four quarters, Salesforce's own revenue grew 11.2%, meaning the buyer is paying for a business growing more than twice as fast as its own. Management said on the September 8, 2026 call that Braze also counted 361 large customers, with each spending at least $500,000 a year.

How Has The Deal Changed What Braze Shares Cost?

Braze shares now cost far more against the company's sales than they did three weeks earlier, and not solely because of the offer. Before the deal news, the stock had already risen about 18% between September 21 and the October 19 close. At the October 20 close, Braze carried a market value of $5.07 billion, or 6.1 times its revenue over the last twelve months. That compares with 3.3 times at the end of September, while the S&P 500 as a whole trades at 3.1 times sales.

The shares closed at $45.57, about 4% below the offer price. That gap suggests the market expects the deal to close but is pricing in some risk or delay.

Braze Still Grows Fast And Still Reports A Loss

Salesforce is buying the business Braze described when it last reported on that September 8 call. Over the twelve months to July 31, 2026, Braze still reported an operating loss equal to 13.4% of revenue, though that loss was narrower than the 20.3% of a year earlier. The company also produced $80.2 million of free cash flow over those twelve months.

During that call, management guided fiscal Q3 2027 revenue to between $229 million and $230 million, up from the $227 million Braze reported for fiscal Q2 2027. They also raised the full-year guide, projecting revenue of $910 million to $913 million for fiscal 2027. The offer changes none of those figures.

We have found that the best way to discover great value opportunities is to pair a strong Zacks Rank with a great grade in the Value category of our Style Scores system. The Zacks Rank favors stocks with strong earnings estimate revision trends, and our Style Scores highlight companies with specific traits.

Value investors are also interested in a number of tried-and-true valuation metrics that help show when a company is undervalued at its current share price levels.

Our Value category grades stocks based on a number of key metrics, including the tried-and-true P/E ratio, the P/S ratio, earnings yield, and cash flow per share, as well as a variety of other fundamentals that value investors frequently use.

CRM currently has a forward P/E ratio of 14.50, while ADSK has a forward P/E of 19.45. We also note that CRM has a PEG ratio of 0.85. This metric is used similarly to the famous P/E ratio, but the PEG ratio also takes into account the stock's expected earnings growth rate. ADSK currently has a PEG ratio of 1.25.

Another notable valuation metric for CRM is its P/B ratio of 5.2. The P/B ratio is used to compare a stock's market value with its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. For comparison, ADSK has a P/B of 15.17.

These are just a few of the metrics contributing to CRM's Value grade of B and ADSK's Value grade of C.

CRM sticks out from ADSK in both our Zacks Rank and Style Scores models, so value investors will likely feel that CRM is the better option right now.

title: Is Veeva Systems Stock Really Expensive?

Is Veeva Systems Stock Really Expensive?

Veeva Systems (VEEV) stock trades at 51 times its earnings over the last twelve months, compared with 23 for the S&P 500. The shares returned 72.7% from July 22 to October 20, 2026. Buyers entering the market after a rally like that are paying today for profit the business has not yet earned. How fast would Veeva have to grow for that price to hold?

Veeva Would Need Faster Growth Than It Delivers

At this price, Veeva would have to grow revenue 18.8% a year for five years. By comparison, revenue grew 16.5% in the twelve months to July 31, 2026. So the shares look somewhat expensive: dear against today's growth, though not by a wide margin.

Three Trefis assumptions dictate that 18.8% rate, none of them observed in the market or stated by the company. Trefis calculates a mature P/E of 22.8 by combining a fixed 18.0 level for healthcare stocks with Veeva's own average P/E. The formula weights the healthcare level at 60% and Veeva's average at 40%. Veeva averaged 49.4 over the last twelve quarter ends. Trefis caps any company average above 30 at 30, so the mature multiple uses 30 in place of Veeva's 49.4.

Veeva closed October 20, 2026, with a market value of $51.7 billion. At the mature P/E, that valuation requires net income of $2.27 billion. Assuming a steady net margin of 27.7%, Veeva would need $8.19 billion in revenue to earn that profit. The 27.7% margin sits halfway between Veeva's 26.1% average and its 29.3% high over the last twelve quarter ends. Trefis allows five years because today's P/E is 2.24 times the mature one, and its rule assigns five years to any ratio from two up to three. Bridging the gap from today's $3.46 billion in revenue to that $8.19 billion target demands 18.8% annual growth.

Does Veeva's Guidance Point To Growth That Fast?

No, not even for fiscal 2027. Management guided revenue of $3.68 billion to $3.69 billion for fiscal 2027, an increase from its June guide of $3.64 billion. The midpoint of that range marks 15.3% growth over fiscal 2026. After fiscal 2027, Veeva would have to grow 19.4% a year until fiscal Q2 2032, faster than the pace management has guided for fiscal 2027. Management said on the August 26 call that it would not guide beyond fiscal 2027.

Subscriptions account for most of the business. The Subscription segment brought in $2.68 billion in fiscal 2026, up 17.5% from a year earlier. On the same call, management said three large companies had selected Vault CRM. Management also raised its fiscal 2027 guide for adjusted operating income to $1.64 billion from $1.61 billion, so the profit outlook rose along with revenue.

Over the last ten years, Microsoft (MSFT) stock turned $10,000 into $92,451 before dividends. That same $10,000 invested in the S&P 500 became $35,968. Looking back makes the strategy seem as simple as buying and waiting, but holding the shares required far more discipline. How many times do you think Microsoft stock fell 20% or more along the way?

How Often Did Microsoft Stock Fall?

Microsoft stock fell 20% or more from a closing high four times. Two of those declines exceeded 30%. All four are listed below.

The deepest drop occurred between November 2021 and November 2022, when the stock fell 37.6% while the S&P 500 lost 20.8%. Investors spent about 19 months below the previous peak until the shares closed above that old high in June 2023. The real question was never just whether to buy Microsoft. It was whether you could sit through falls like these.

What Did Holding Microsoft Through A Fall Feel Like?

The most recent decline began at a closing high on October 28, 2025, and the stock took nearly eight months to reach its low on June 25, 2026, dropping 34.9%. The S&P 500 rose 6.8% over those same months, so shareholders lost ground while the broader market gained.

From that low, the stock took another 3.6 months to close above its old high. All four of Microsoft's declines eventually ended. Nobody holding shares in the middle of a drop knew that at the time, however, and an investor in the spring of 2026 had no way to know this one would.

Was Something Wrong With Microsoft's Business?

Microsoft generates revenue from cloud services such as Azure and software such as Microsoft 365. Its two largest segments are Intelligent Cloud, followed by Productivity and Business Processes. During the deepest fall, revenue over twelve months rose 15.2%, and the operating margin stayed close to 42% from the high to the low.

In the latest fall, which was shorter, twelve-month revenue rose 8.3% from the high to the low, and the operating margin edged up from 46.3% to 46.8%.

Sales grew and operating margins held steady during both falls while the stock declined. A drop like that, while the business keeps growing, is the risk of holding the shares.

What Selling Microsoft Stock Would Have Cost

Microsoft stock is up 148.2% since its November 2022 low, and anyone who sold there missed all of it. Today, the stock sits 2.1% below the high it set on October 13, 2026.

How Has Zoom's Story Changed?

Zoom Communications (ZM) stock trades at 5.7 times sales, against 3.1 for the S&P 500. Shareholders paying that premium need to know what they are buying, and Zoom has changed how it describes what it sells. On the fiscal Q3 2025 call in November 2024, management described moving Zoom from a unified communication and collaboration platform into an AI-first work platform. The pitch has since moved on again. So what does management talk up now?

Zoom Now Pitches An AI-First System Of Action

On the fiscal Q2 2027 call in August 2026, management said customers are choosing Zoom as an AI-first, integrated, multi-product system of action. The company wants to use its position in live communications to capture context and intent. It highlighted ZoomMate, launched in June, as the product that turns conversations into completed work. The word collaboration came up only twice on that call, though AI in Zoom Workplace, the collaboration suite, was one of its three priorities.

Six months after that November 2024 call, the tools themselves were still part of the pitch. On the fiscal Q1 2026 call in May 2025, management said Zoom Workplace continued to drive customers to adopt other Zoom solutions. The collaboration suite served as the way into the rest of Zoom. Those tools have not left the story. On the fiscal Q1 2027 call, management called Zoom Workplace the foundation of its system of action. The collaboration tools are now the base Zoom builds AI on, rather than the product it emphasizes.

When Zoom Communications is a large share of what you own, what its management stops saying matters more. See how to protect a concentrated position.

How Big Is Zoom's Enterprise Business Now?

Zoom's enterprise business accounted for 62% of revenue in fiscal Q2 2027. Enterprise revenue grew 7.8% from a year earlier, marking its strongest growth rate in three years. Total revenue reached $1.28 billion, up 4.9%, putting enterprise sales at about $0.79 billion for the quarter.

Management credited that speed-up to its three AI priorities: AI in Zoom Workplace, an AI-first customer experience and new AI products. Adoption of these AI tools is also spreading. Licensed monthly active users of AI features in Zoom Workplace grew 125% from a year earlier, and the customer count for Zoom Virtual Agent increased more than 250%.

Should Zoom Holders Find The New Pitch Reassuring?

So far it looks reassuring, because management credits the AI push for faster enterprise growth, and use of the AI tools is rising. Management raised its revenue forecast for fiscal 2027 to 4.5% growth at the midpoint, up from 4.1% at the start of the year. The company's backlog of billed and unbilled contracts also rose 14% to about $4.5 billion.

title: Salesforce to acquire Braze for $5.66bn in customer experience push
detail:
Salesforce to acquire Braze for $5.66bn in customer experience push
Anwesha Pattanaik
Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:50 AM MST 3 min read
BRZE
CRM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Salesforce has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Braze, a US-headquartered cloud-based software company, in a transaction valued at approximately $5.66bn.

Under the agreed terms, holders of Braze Class A common stock will receive $47.50 in cash per share. Braze is currently listed on Nasdaq.

The acquisition is expected to close in Salesforce's fiscal year (FY) 2028, pending approval from Braze shareholders and regulatory authorities.

Braze provides tools for marketers to personalise customer interactions across mobile applications, websites, SMS, email, WhatsApp, and other channels.

The company operates an event-streaming architecture designed for real-time business-to-consumer engagement, maintaining up-to-date customer profiles and supporting large volumes of messages and journey actions each year.

Additional capabilities are offered through BrazeAI, which uses AI to optimise content, channels, offers, and message timing.

Salesforce applications and marketing president Patrick Stokes said: "Every interaction is an opportunity to wow your customers. Most of that wow comes from knowing your customer, and responding at just the right moment.

"Braze was built to turn live customer behaviour into personalised engagement at scale. Bringing that capability together with Salesforce Marketing Cloud, CRM, and Data 360 will deliver that wow moment in every customer interaction."

Salesforce indicated that Braze's technology is expected to strengthen areas such as Data 360, Marketing Cloud, and other components of Salesforce's Customer 360 platform.

The integration is anticipated to support expanded cross-channel personalisation and real-time engagement for brands aiming to reach large audiences.

Braze CEO and co-founder Bill Magnuson said: "Braze was built on the conviction that marketers and their creativity are a brand's ultimate competitive advantage. This past year we shipped at the fastest pace in our history, and BrazeAI is helping marketers get their best ideas live faster.

"Salesforce shares our commitment to marketers, and we'll continue building as Braze and investing in the Braze community of customers and partners who built this company with us.

"Salesforce's platform will help us innovate faster and together we'll help marketers around the world build deeper, more lasting relationships with their customers."

Braze currently serves around 2,770 customers, including companies such as Canva, Equinox, Dairy Queen, Urban Outfitters, Instacart, and Venmo.

The company was co-founded by Bill Magnuson and Jon Hyman, and brings expertise in mobile engagement and data engineering.
